CRITICAL REVIEW: 2026-11-12-package-hallucination-and-slopsquatting (9 analyses, all status: ready)
No files were written, as the caller instructed. Each analysis was checked against its fulltext.txt (page markers) and metadata.json, and `rlab validate` and `rlab cite-check` were run.

SUMMARY: 0 pass, 8 pass-with-minor-fixes, 1 fail (okwor2026hallucination: provenance blocked). cite-check: OK for all 9. validate: verified for 8. okwor2026hallucination = MISMATCH.

Systemic format issue: zhao2025hfuzzer, haque2025secure, zheng2026when, dasu2026refusing and zhang2025llm write evidence-table labels as bare V/A/I. The other four use [V]/[A]/[I]. These five also leave the §2 RQ lists and §6 metric lines unlabelled. Fix: use brackets everywhere, label the RQ lines [A] and the metric lines [V].

======================================================================
1. spracklen2024we: PASS-WITH-MINOR-FIXES
Provenance: verified, PDF identity matched (arXiv v3). Number check: 14 values grepped (19.7%, 440,445, 205,474, 5.2/21.7, 15.8/21.3, 43/39/58%, 81%, 13.4/48.6%, 0.17%, 8.7%, 8.9/31.8%, +1.16%, Table 4/5 values). All appear on the cited pages.

1.1 §7 finding 2 and the §13 RQ1 row.
- Current text: "Lowest overall: GPT-4 Turbo at 3.59%. Lowest open model: DeepSeek 1B at 13.63%".
- What the paper says: the text calls these "overall" (p. 7), but they are the Python-only values in Table 7 (p. 20). The JavaScript values in Table 8 are GPT-4 Turbo 4.00% and DeepSeek 1B 27.45%. DeepSeek 1B is among the worst JavaScript models.
- Correction: "[V] GPT-4 Turbo 3.59% and DeepSeek 1B 13.63% are reported as overall/best (p. 7), but they match the Python column of Table 7 (p. 20). JavaScript: GPT-4 Turbo 4.00%, DeepSeek 1B 27.45% (Table 8, p. 20). [I] The 'overall' labels in the text are Python-only."
- This matters because churilov2026range uses 3.59% as its benchmark.

1.2 §6 and §7 findings 2–3.
- Problem: the analysis does not say how the class and language figures are aggregated.
- Our recomputation from Tables 7–8 (p. 20): 5.2% is the unweighted mean of the 6 GPT model-language rates, 21.7% the unweighted mean of the 24 open-model tests, and 15.8% / 21.3% the unweighted means of the per-model rates. Only 19.7% is pooled over mentions.
- Add: "[I] Our recomputation from Tables 7–8 shows that 5.2%, 21.7%, 15.8% and 21.3% are unweighted means of per-test mention rates. Only 19.7% is a pooled mention rate (p. 7)."

1.3 §4 Sampling.
- Current text: "RQ2–RQ4 use only Python, 4 models ... and randomly sampled subsets".
- Paper: this is the authors' statement (p. 7). However, the recency analysis covers "all 16 Python models" (p. 8, Fig. 4), and the cross-model analysis covers 16 tests (p. 10, p. 12).
- Correction: label it [A] and add "[V] Some RQ2/RQ4 analyses nevertheless use all 16 Python models (recency, p. 8; cross-model overlap, p. 10)."

1.4 §3 Mitigation, fine-tuning.
- Current text: "560,000 H1/H2 response pairs".
- Paper (pp. 12–13): "code/package list (Heuristic 1) and prompt/package list (Heuristic 2)". By the paper's own definitions on pp. 6–7, those are H2 and H3.
- Correction: "...pairs the paper labels H1/H2, although by its own definitions (p. 6–7) they correspond to H2 (code→packages) and H3 (prompt→packages)".

1.5 §4 Data availability.
- Current text: "[V] Code, both prompt datasets ... are released".
- Paper, p. 14: "will make ... publicly available" (a promise).
- Correction: "[A] promised (p. 14); release of the prompt datasets and package lists is confirmed by [@churilov2026range, p. 15, p. 17]."

1.6 §5 Decoding sweep.
- Current text: "Top-k and min-p were tested only on the open models".
- Paper, p. 8: "only tested for DeepSeek and CodeLlama".
- Correct to that wording.

1.7 §5 appraisal is missing funding.
- Paper, p. 14: UTSA Faculty Development Leave and NSF award 2231002; findings disclosed to OpenAI, Meta, DeepSeek and Mistral.
- Add: "Funding: UTSA FDL, NSF 2231002 (p. 14); no COI statement."

1.8 Header and venue.
- Metadata says venue_kind: preprint. USENIX Security '25 is supported by [@churilov2026range, p. 1, p. 16] and [@okwor2026hallucination, p. 9]. Standards §3 say to use the published version when one exists.
- Fix:
  - Remove "according to the project lead" (not evidence).
  - Keep the two citations.
  - State the tier as "tier 1 (published, USENIX Security 2025), analysed from the arXiv v3 text".
  - Log the decision with `rlab log`. metadata.json cannot be hand-edited; if `rlab add` cannot resolve the USENIX version (it has no DOI), say so in Analyst notes.

======================================================================
2. churilov2026range: PASS-WITH-MINOR-FIXES
Provenance: verified (identity "probable"). Number check: 20 values grepped (3.63–5.02, 2.15–3.39, 7/10 and 8/10, +2.34/+3.47, 4.79/5.44/2.28/3.10, Jaccard 0.219/0.173/0.342, 104/88/16, 2,699, 54, p = 0.012, 144–207, 25/2,282, 0/87 vs 2/101, CI −6.9 to +2.5, 1,746/536, 39,969/39,964, 1.27/31.51%, 14,821, 10.5%, 1,157). All match pp. 1–17.

2.1 §3 Baselines and §9 bullet 1.
- Current text: "Spracklen's 2024 figures: 3.59% best model, 5.2% commercial average, 21.7% open-source average".
- Paper: Churilov compares pooled Python+JavaScript per-model rates with 3.59% (pp. 6, 13). 3.59% is Spracklen's Python-only GPT-4 Turbo value ([@spracklen2024we, p. 20], Table 7). Since Churilov finds Python > JavaScript, the comparison is not like-for-like even before extraction differences.
- Add to §9: "[I] The 'level with Spracklen's best model' claim compares a pooled Py+JS rate (Haiku 3.63%) with Spracklen's Python-only 3.59% ([@spracklen2024we, p. 20]). Churilov's own Python-only Haiku rate is 4.38% (Table 2, p. 7). Spracklen's 5.2% and 21.7% are unweighted means of per-test rates."

2.2 §7 finding 2.
- Current text: "Gemini, DeepSeek and GPT-5.4-mini do not differ significantly from each other".
- Paper, Table 4 (p. 8): this holds only at the mention level. All three pairs are significant at the generation level.
- Correction: "...at the mention level; all three pairs differ significantly at the generation level (Table 4, p. 8)."

2.3 §7 finding 4 does not flag a reversal of Spracklen on the same prompt corpus.
- Churilov (Table 3, p. 7): LLM-written prompts give higher rates than Stack Overflow prompts for every model.
- Spracklen: Stack Overflow > LLM-generated for nearly every model (e.g. CodeLlama 7B Python 32.53% vs 21.51%) ([@spracklen2024we, p. 20]).
- Add: "[I] This reverses Spracklen's prompt-source ordering on the same prompt corpus; record it as a contradiction."

2.4 §5 / §10 appraisal is missing funding and COI.
- Paper, p. 15: self-funded plus a Google Cloud credit grant; "no conflicts of interest"; Claude was used for analysis code and drafting.
- Add these.

2.5 §4 Dataset.
- Add: "[V] The released corpus has 39,969 prompts (20,163 SO + 19,806 LLM) (p. 4)."
- Add: "[I] Spracklen describes 2 × 19,200 (p. 6) or 19,500 prompts (p. 2). The released corpus therefore does not match Spracklen's stated counts; keep this in mind when replicating."

======================================================================
3. okwor2026hallucination: FAIL (blocking provenance; the content fixes are minor)
Number check: 12 values grepped (839,365 / 4,194,421, 4,800 + 2,000, 1,186 + 455 = 1,641, 82, 0.228 / 0.247, 450 / 455, 22 / 149, 19 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 0, 17 + 8 holdout, 11 negative-control names, 2026-07-04). All are on pp. 3–7.

3.1 Header (provenance).
- `rlab validate` returns MISMATCH: Crossref "not found", OpenAlex ok. The PDF prints DOI ...21199427 (p. 1); the metadata has ...21199426.
- The analysis never states the validate status.
- Required:
  - Record "validate: MISMATCH (Crossref has no record; Zenodo DOIs are DataCite; OpenAlex matches)".
  - Resolve both DOIs via doi.org to confirm they are the concept and version records of the same deposit.
  - Log the outcome with `rlab log`.
  - Do not mark the analysis complete until this is done.

3.2 §7 finding 7.
- Current text: "[V] The npm name mirror is unreliable: it lists more names than npm's own total, yet misses real packages registered years ago (p. 3)".
- Paper, p. 3: no counts are given. The only data are the 11 negative-control names (p. 7).
- Correction: "[A] (p. 3); partly supported by the 11 negative-control names that predate t0 (2014–2023) and that the mirror missed [V] (p. 7)."

3.3 §7 finding 4 (attribution of the 19 placeholders to one operator).
- Labelled [V].
- Paper, p. 6: the evidence "lives in the withheld registry metadata ... verifiable only from that data, which we can provide to reviewers under embargo".
- Correction: change to [A] and add "(evidence withheld, p. 6)". Only the shared summary string is [V] (p. 5).

3.4 §7 finding 5.
- Scope missing.
- Correction: "Of the 2,000 extra generations, 11 produced names absent from the snapshot but live (p. 7). The author calls this 'essentially uninformative' given the few-day window (p. 7)."

3.5 Missing RQ2-relevant content.
- Paper, p. 2: Lanyado's registered hallucinated name `huggingface-cli` drew more than 30,000 downloads in three months; a hallucinated npm name spread to 237 GitHub repositories before a researcher defensively claimed it.
- Add as "[A] secondary claims citing grey sources [4, 5] (p. 2); not verified by this paper". Our RQ2 asks directly about real-world slopsquatting.

3.6 §5 Code availability.
- Current text: "Not yet available (p. 8)".
- Paper, p. 8: "will be deposited". We did not check whether it has been.
- Correction: "[A] promised (p. 8); we did not check whether the deposit exists."

3.7 Header tier.
- The analysis says tier 4 (grey literature). The paper self-labels "Preprint, July 2026" (p. 1). Under standards §3 that is tier 3, with a company affiliation.
- Either tier is defensible. State the reason (single author, company-affiliated, Zenodo self-deposit, no peer review) so the tier choice is not arbitrary.

======================================================================
4. krishna2025importing: PASS-WITH-MINOR-FIXES
Number check: 14 values grepped (Table 3 cells, 14.73/23.14/24.74, σ 16.03/14.37/8.43, r = −0.542 / p = 0.00114, −0.593 / 0.00028, −0.7887, −0.2919, Table 4 means, Table 2 counts, Mamba 21.03 vs Llama-8B 15.24, "15 billion", µ = 26.90%). All are correct. We recomputed the Python mean from Table 3: 254.51 / 11 = 23.14.

4.1 §10 External.
- Current text: "[V] This is the only study in our set that covers Rust and crates.io (p. 4)".
- This is false: zheng2026when is Rust-only, dasu2026refusing has nonexistent-crate prompts, and spracklen2024we checks Cargo for cross-language names (p. 11).
- Correction: "[V] Covers Rust/crates.io alongside JS and Python (p. 4). [I] Within the project, Rust is also covered by [@zheng2026when] and [@dasu2026refusing]."

4.2 §4 Sample size: the estimate can be confirmed from the data.
- The smallest PHR, 0.22%, equals 1/455; the largest, 46.15%, equals 210/455 (Table 3, p. 4). This fits 7 stubs × 13 tasks × 5 repeats = 455 prompts per model-language cell.
- Add: "[I] Table 3 values are multiples of 1/455, which supports N = 455 per model-language cell. Nemotron's 0.22% is a single prompt."

4.3 §6 / §9 statistics: a missing threat.
- Table 1 (p. 3): GPT-4o's size, "200B*", is "an approximation, from Abacha et al. (2024)" (a medical-benchmark paper). GPT-4o is the extreme x-value in the size correlation.
- Add: "[I] The size correlation depends on an unverified 200B estimate for GPT-4o (Table 1 footnote, p. 3)."

4.4 §7 finding 3, "Best models".
- Dracarys has the lowest Python PHR, 2.42% (Table 3, p. 4; text p. 5), lower than GPT-4o (3.52%) and Nemotron (4.84%).
- Add: "Lowest Python: Dracarys 2.42%."

======================================================================
5. zhao2025hfuzzer: PASS-WITH-MINOR-FIXES
Provenance: published at ASE 2025 (verified). Number check: 13 values grepped (2.60×, 4.89×, 5.13×, 0.26–0.66%, 5.68/7.10/9.82/16.47%, 3.02×, 190/176, 17, 2.36×/2.46×, ablation 2.06/1.39/1.27 and 4.40/1.25/1.26, 46/34/12, k-parameters). All are on pp. 1–9.

5.1 §5 and §9 bullet 1.
- Current text: "the registry query date is not reported".
- Paper: reference [13] "Pypi ... last accessed Mar. 2025" (p. 12).
- Correction: "Registry query date not stated; PyPI 'last accessed Mar. 2025' in reference [13] (p. 12) is the best proxy."

5.2 §13 RQ4 row.
- Current text: "34 of 46 ... arise at the install-command stage with correct imports; import-regex extraction misses them" [V].
- The "misses them" part is the authors' hypothesis (p. 9). It is also not strictly true: an import-regex extractor without import→package mapping would extract `pywt` too (same string), for a different reason.
- Correction: split the row. "[V] 34 of 46 are package errors with correct imports (p. 9)" and "[A] import-based extraction overlooks install-stage hallucinations (p. 9)".

5.3 §13 RQ3 row.
- Mixes [V] data with our proposal ("comment-aware filtering is a possible cheap check").
- Correction: keep "[V] 12 cases (p. 9)" and move the suggestion to §11 as [I].

5.4 §7 finding 12.
- Current text: "temperature shows no clear trend".
- Paper, p. 10: the temperature tested is that of the tester model, on two combinations only.
- Correction: "tester-model temperature (two combinations) shows no clear trend (p. 10)."

5.5 §3: β is printed as "0.51" in the text layer (p. 4); this is a footnote marker attached to 0.5. The analysis has 0.5, which is correct. No change; noted for anyone re-quoting.

======================================================================
6. haque2025secure: PASS-WITH-MINOR-FIXES
Number check: all Table 1 cells cited (PHR and VPR, including the Paraphrase VPR column 15.57→8.22 and 12.30→9.57), Table 2 counts and the p. 7 discussion figures. All are correct. Table 2's 1.5B 4-bit SO row sums to 7,550 with 4,751 hallucinated = 62.93%, consistent with Table 1.

6.1 §7 finding 6 and the §13 RQ2 row.
- Current text: "[V] Hallucinated strings are mostly URL-like Go module paths".
- Paper, p. 6: "the LLM generated package strings mostly in the url category". That refers to all generated strings, and "Across all models" cannot be checked because only one table (1.5B 4-bit) is printed. In that table, URL categories account for 2,418 of 4,751 hallucinated SO strings (51%); file paths (1,372) and "other" (961) make up 49% (Table 2, p. 8).
- Correction: "[A] Generated strings are mostly URLs, mainly github.com/golang.org (p. 6). [V] In the only table shown (1.5B 4-bit, SO), 2,418 of 4,751 (51%) hallucinated strings are URLs and 2,333 (49%) are file paths or free-form strings (Table 2, p. 8)."

6.2 §9 bullet 3: strengthen with the number above.
- Add: "[I] About half of 'hallucinated packages' in the one cell shown are not installable module paths, so PHR overstates squattable names."

6.3 §3: "One generation pass per prompt is implied" has no label. Mark it [I].

======================================================================
7. zheng2026when: PASS-WITH-MINOR-FIXES
Number check: 18 values grepped (22.23%, 10,779/48,494, 16,764, 16.18/26.90, 1.66, 23.34/20.79/25.23, Table 2 range 18.46–21.92, F-tests, 45.47%, "over half", 1,086/828, Jaccard 0.44/0.16, 55.05/25.42%, 5,647/13,332, 3.42/40.78/86.48/2.36/32.96%, 38.9%, Table 4 deltas). All are correct. The p. 1 quote is verified (lines 47–48).

7.1 Header venue.
- Current text: "An acceptance at Internetware 2026 was reported to us as an author claim".
- This is unsourced: the PDF does not mention it, and metadata says arXiv.
- Correction: delete it, or move it to Analyst notes as "unverified venue claim from [source]; not in PDF or metadata". If a published version exists, resolve it with `rlab add`.

7.2 §5: name normalisation not addressed.
- Cargo treats `-` and `_` as equivalent (a crate is published as `tokio-util` and referenced as `tokio_util`). The paper does not report how source identifiers were matched to crates.io names. It does report a hyphen-omission pattern (32.96%, p. 7).
- Add: "Hyphen/underscore normalisation between source identifiers and crates.io names: not reported. [I] Without it, hyphenated crates would be counted as hallucinations; with it, the hyphen-omission finding needs re-checking."

7.3 §7 finding 7 [A] contrast with prior work.
- Units differ. Zheng's 40.78% / 86.48% are occurrence-weighted ("hallucination occurrences", p. 7). Spracklen's 13.4% / 48.6% are over 76,489 unique Python names ([@spracklen2024we, p. 11]).
- Add: "[I] Not directly comparable: occurrence-weighted (Rust, non-module) vs unique names (Python)."

7.4 §5: the main run used the largest open sizes from Ollama (p. 5), including DeepSeek-Coder-V2 236B. The "to be checked" quantization caveat applies to all open models in RQ1 too, not only the size sweep. Extend §9 bullet 6 accordingly.

======================================================================
8. dasu2026refusing: PASS-WITH-MINOR-FIXES
Number check: 20 values grepped (54/31/15%, 1/1,547, HR range 0.23–0.90, Table IV and Table V cells, Spearman values, 100% for DeepSeek-V3.2 and gpt-oss 120B, 94/87/76/63/63/33% and 87/84/68/50/50/15%, 14% vs 94%, B1–B4 shares, 47/43/18%, 0.64 vs 0.43, CI 8–34, 34% vs 15%, 33/270, 11, pywfm, 28/23/5, judge κ values, 12 npm + 10 crate prompts on p. 9). All are correct.

8.1 §13 RQ2 row "33 of 270 prompts fool at least 16 of 17 models".
- Mapping problem: in the plausible-entity family the package name is planted by the prompt (p. 3; p. 10 "we plant a name"). Cross-model "repetition" of that name is trivially the planted name, so this is not evidence that invented names are predictable.
- Correction: re-map the row to RQ1/RQ4 (prompt-driven acceptance), or add "[I] names are supplied by the prompt; not evidence of spontaneous cross-model name repetition".

8.2 §13 RQ3 row "18% of plausible-entity hallucinations are 'factual' ... and would evade registry checks" [V].
- Paper, p. 7: these responses use "only real packages and APIs"; "no registry check will notice" is the authors' wording.
- [I] These responses install no nonexistent package, so they carry no slopsquatting risk. Using them as evidence against registry-check defences is misleading for our RQ3.
- Correction: "[V] 18% are factual (p. 7). [A] 'no registry check will notice' (p. 7). [I] These responses install no fictitious package, so they do not bear on slopsquatting defences."

8.3 §13 RQ2 row "Misspelled real package names are caught 86% of the time".
- Paper, p. 8: a misspelled name is "fabricated on 14% of prompts". The remaining 86% are correct (typo fixed) or refusals (p. 4 rule).
- Correction: "fabricated on 14% (vs 94% for fictional names); the rest are corrected or refused (p. 4, p. 8)."

8.4 §7 finding 3.
- Add the per-group counts: small = 4 models, mid = 8, large = 5 (Table V, p. 6).
- Add: "[I] The npm+crates subset has 22 prompts per model, so 1.00 / 0.90 / 0.85 rest on 88 / 176 / 110 responses."

======================================================================
9. zhang2025llm: PASS-WITH-MINOR-FIXES
Number check: taxonomy shares (43.53 = 36.66 + 6.86; 31.91 = 8.82 + 2.68 + 20.41; 24.56 = 0.94 + 11.26 + 12.36), Table I Pass@1, 1,380 seed snippets and temperature 0.6. All are correct (pp. 3–9).

9.1 Venue (the caller's premise is not supported).
- The caller wrote "PACMSE/FSE 2025". Three project papers cite this work as Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering vol. 2, issue ISSTA (2025), pp. 481–503:
  - [@zheng2026when, p. 11];
  - [@dasu2026refusing, p. 11] ("in ISSTA, 2025");
  - liu2026mitigating fulltext line 766–767.
- The analysis's ISSTA attribution is the evidenced one. Do not change it to FSE unless the DOI landing page says otherwise.

CROSS-PAPER NOTES FOR THE EVIDENCE MATRIX
(evidence-matrix.md is currently empty, 13 lines.)

A. Rate units: never pool or rank these figures across papers.
- spracklen2024we: mention-level (hallucinated names / all names). It pools H1 install commands in code with H2/H3 answers the model gives when asked directly. Only 19.7% is pooled. 5.2% / 21.7% / 15.8% / 21.3% are unweighted means of per-test rates. 3.59% and 13.63% are Python-only.
- churilov2026range: mention-level (install commands plus `ast`/tree-sitter imports with pipreqs mapping) and generation-level (≥1 hallucination per generation). One sample per prompt; live registry with a time-of-generation rule.
- krishna2025importing: per prompt (≥1 hallucinated import), N = 455 per model-language cell. Regex imports with no mapping and no stdlib filter. A date-aware definition counts post-cutoff registrations as hallucinations.
- zhao2025hfuzzer: per response (Krishna's definition), on fuzzer-optimised tasks. Names come from the model's own install-command answer (similar to Spracklen H2). Counts other-language and post-cutoff names. Not a base rate.
- haque2025secure: per Go package string; reachability oracle; about half of hallucinations in the one table shown are file paths or free text.
- zheng2026when: per source-level crate reference; 45.47% are std/module confusions; not install-level.
- dasu2026refusing: acceptance of a planted fictitious name per prompt. A different construct from spontaneous invention.
- okwor2026hallucination: no rate (distinct names and yield per generation only).
- zhang2025llm: category shares of hallucination instances only.

B. Extraction method, to record in a matrix column:
- Model-queried: Spracklen H2/H3; Zhao stage 2.
- Install-command parsing: Spracklen H1, Churilov, Haque.
- Import parsing: Churilov (pipreqs, ~1,157 names), Okwor (mapping, source unreported), Krishna (none), Zheng (crate aliases; `-`/`_` handling unreported).
- Spracklen explicitly rejects import parsing, but Churilov says it "follow[s] Spracklen's extraction approach" (p. 5). The 2024→2026 comparison is therefore not like-for-like.

C. Contradictions, for the Contradictions section (each needs data, method and time compared; any explanation labelled [I]):
1. Language.
   - Spracklen: JS > Py (unweighted means 21.3 vs 15.8, p. 7).
   - Krishna: JS lowest (14.73 vs Py 23.14, p. 8).
   - Churilov: Py > JS for every model (p. 7).
   - Candidate explanation [I]: import-based Python extraction plus module/package name mismatch, different cohorts.
2. Prompt source, same corpus.
   - Spracklen: SO > LLM-generated ([@spracklen2024we, p. 20]).
   - Churilov: LLM-generated > SO for every model ([@churilov2026range, p. 7]).
   - Same prompt sets, opposite ordering. This is the cleanest contradiction in the set.
3. Model size.
   - Krishna: larger models are better, but significance rests on n = 33 pseudo-replicates and a guessed 200B for GPT-4o.
   - Zheng: no size effect in Rust (F(1,4) = 0.0138).
   - Dasu: scale helps on impossibilities but barely on nonexistent packages.
   - Churilov: Haiku < Sonnet.
   - Zhao: Llama-3.1 > Llama-3.
4. Temperature.
   - Spracklen: rises sharply above 1 (p. 8).
   - Zheng: no effect from 0 to 2 in Rust (p. 6).
   - Zhao's temperature result is for the tester model and is not comparable.
5. Edit distance.
   - Spracklen: 13.4% within 1–2 edits and 48.6% at 6 or more (unique Python names).
   - Zheng: 40.78% within 1–2 and 86.48% within 5 (occurrence-weighted, Rust non-module).
   - Churilov: 54 of 104 universal names at distance 1.
   - Different units; do not present as a direct contradiction without saying so.
6. Cross-model overlap.
   - Spracklen: 81% of names come from a single model.
   - Churilov: mean Jaccard 0.219 and 104 universal names.
   - Okwor: 82 of 1,186 names multi-model; 450 of 455 new names single-model.
   - Zhao: 190 + 176 shared names.
   - Zheng: non-module Jaccard about 0.16.
   - Consistent picture: mostly model-specific, with a persistent shared core.
7. Mitigation effect sizes.
   - Spracklen (Python): RAG 26.28→13.40 on CodeLlama.
   - Zheng (Rust): RAG −0.34 to +1.92 points; self-refinement 2.22 to 3.26 points.
   - Same method families, very different magnitudes.

D. Registration / real-world exploitation (RQ2). These findings are compatible, not contradictory.
- Churilov: 25 of 2,282 names registered within about 6 months; 1 registered with malware; 23 suggested names with a malware history; 22 registrations not inspected.
- Okwor: 0 of 1,641 private names registered after 4 days; 22 of 149 public-list names registered, 0 malicious, 19 from one benign-placeholder operator.
- [I] Churilov's uninspected registrations may include defensive placeholders of the kind Okwor found.
- Okwor's huggingface-cli and npm examples are secondary [A] claims (p. 2).

E. Do not reuse secondary citations.
- Okwor misreports Spracklen's 21.7% as "of generations" and quotes superseded Churilov v1–3 figures (4.62–6.10% "per generation", 127 names, 53 registrable) as current. Those v1–3 rates were mention-level ([@churilov2026range, p. 6, p. 10–11]).
- Always cite the primary source.

F. Hidden quantization confound.
- Spracklen ran all open models with GPTQ (p. 6).
- Dasu ran models ≤32B at 4-bit and larger ones at full precision (p. 10).
- Zheng used Ollama models with unreported quantization.
- Haque varies quantization explicitly (Go, bitsandbytes).
- Any "size" finding involving open models may be partly a precision effect.

G. Independence and venues.
- Churilov reuses Spracklen's prompts, and earlier versions also used Spracklen's package lists, so it is not an independent prompt sample.
- Peer-reviewed: spracklen2024we (USENIX Sec '25, arXiv text analysed), zhao2025hfuzzer (ASE '25), zhang2025llm (PACMSE ISSTA '25, arXiv text analysed).
- Everything else is a preprint. okwor2026hallucination is a single-author Zenodo deposit from a company.
- No paper in this batch measures agentic tools that install dependencies automatically. That gap still needs a novelty check under §7.
